author: Linnaeus, 1758
status: 겨울에 드물게 찾아옴, 지금까지 기록 10건 미만
summary: 매우 드물게 찾아오는 겨울철새로, 평야, 구릉지, 초원과 농경지에서 지낸다. 긴 목과 다리에 통통하고 큰 몸집이라 쉽게 알아볼 수 있다. 한 수컷이 여러 암컷과 짝을 짓는 일부다처제로 산다. 예전에는 흔한 겨울철새였으나 불법 사냥과 농약 사용, 잇따른 개발로 위협받고 있다.

art.subject: Great Bustard (Otis tarda), adult male of the eastern population (Otis tarda dybowskii) in winter, as on Korean farmland from November to February: head and upper neck grey; a rufous-chestnut band across the lower neck and upper breast; upperparts golden-buff to cinnamon, densely barred black; white wing coverts showing along the lower edge of the folded wing; underparts white. Bill short, stout, greyish horn; iris dark; legs grey-brown.
art.pose: walking slowly across an open field
art.scene: Korean winter farmland and rolling grassy plain; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male winter, side view standing: grey head and neck, rufous-chestnut band across the lower neck and breast, golden-buff back densely barred black, white along the folded wing and on the belly, heavy plump body on long sturdy legs
adult male, front view standing: broad rufous-chestnut band across the breast below the thick grey neck, white belly, short stout bill
adult male, flight seen from above: long broad wings with a large white panel, black primaries and a dark trailing edge, contrasting with the barred golden-buff back
art.build: Very large, heavy ground bird; the male is larger than a goose and far heavier, the female much smaller and slimmer. Thick neck held upright, broad deep chest and heavy body carried horizontally. Head rounded. Bill short and stout, shorter than the head, chicken-like. Legs long and thick, with three short forward toes and no hind toe. Wings folded on the back at rest; in flight long, broad wings with a large white panel, black primaries and a dark trailing edge, beaten in slow, powerful strokes. Tail short.
avoid: Do not give this winter bird the long white whisker plumes or the puffed-out display neck of spring males.
Do not paint a slender, crane-like bird; it is heavy and broad-chested, with the body held horizontal.
Do not paint a long bill; the bill is short and chicken-like.
Do not paint a hind toe; bustards have only three forward toes.
